public_rationale: Large commitments alone do not establish inability to pay them when due. The records also show substantial financing and reported liquidity, which must enter the comparison. The available evidence does not supply a matched payment-and-funding assessment for both labs or establish the exclusive causal explanation. The claim's accounting basis is unspecified.
limitations: OpenAI liquidity reporting is secondary and predates the target quarter.
Anthropic's later filing cannot by itself settle the position of both companies.
Funding raised is neither revenue nor necessarily cash still available.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Neither OpenAI nor Anthropic has the money to pay for their obligations, and they have only been able to keep up because signing contracts costs little.

statement.excerpt: In any case, neither OpenAI nor Anthropic actually have the money to pay for their obligations, and have only been able to keep up because of the low cost of signing contracts.

from_speaker: actually have the money to pay for their obligations
only been able to keep up
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading concerns each company's ability to fund contractual payments when due, not whether today's cash covers every future payment immediately.
Use April–June 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter that could have been reported before publication, for the financial position underlying this ongoing claim.
The word 'only' requires evidence that small initial payments were necessary to remaining current, after accounting for financing and operating cash receipts.
The passage does not identify an accounting basis for its liquidity comparison.
criteria.support_condition: For both companies, matched liquidity and payment schedules show insufficient available funds for obligations as they fall due, and demonstrate that deferred or small initial payments explain their ability to remain current.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched records show that either company could fund the relevant scheduled obligations, or establish that keeping current did not depend on small initial payments.
